findings.title: validateHandlerOrder overflow bypass: sqrtPriceX96=0 passes max pricing bound
confidence_deductions: requires token admin to set only max bound (no min)
handler orders go through CLOB which has additional constraints
findings.description: When SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 overflows and returns 0, validateHandlerOrder does not check for sqrtPriceX96==0 (unlike _validatePricingBounds at line 847). A handler order with an extreme price ratio that causes overflow bypasses max pricing bounds when min is not set. The check '0 > maxSqrtPriceX96' is always false.
findings.impact: Token creator who sets only a max price ceiling gets no protection when a handler creates an order with an astronomical price ratio. CLOB orders placed at effectively infinite prices.
findings.proof_sketch: test_H02_overflowPriceBypassesMaxBound: sets max bound, calls validateHandlerOrder with amounts causing overflow -> no revert
findings.victim: Token creators setting max-only pricing bounds
findings.extractable_value: Depends on CLOB fill mechanics - order may never fill at extreme prices
attack_sequence: Token admin sets max pricing bound for their token (min=0, max=1e30)
Attacker calls validateHandlerOrder with amountIn=1, amountOut=type(uint256).max/2
Check '0 > maxSqrtPriceX96' fails silently - order accepted at infinite price
prerequisites: Token with only max pricing bound set (no min)

findings.title: validateHandlerOrder bypasses all trading rules (pause, whitelist, direct swap block)
confidence_deductions: by-design: validateHandlerOrder is intentionally minimal for handler use
impact limited to CLOB order placement, not execution
findings.description: validateHandlerOrder has NO access control and performs NO trading rule checks (tradingIsPaused, blockDirectSwaps, pairedTokenWhitelist). Only pricing bounds are enforced. In contrast, beforeSwap/afterSwap enforce all trading rules. CLOB orders can be placed while trading is paused.
findings.impact: Token admin who pauses trading expects ALL activity to halt, but CLOB makers can continue placing orders. Orders placed during pause may fill when trading resumes.
findings.proof_sketch: test_H04_handlerOrderBypassesTradingPause: pauses trading, validateHandlerOrder succeeds, beforeSwap reverts
findings.victim: Token admins relying on trading pause for emergency stops
findings.extractable_value: Indirect - front-running advantage from placing orders during pause
attack_sequence: Token admin pauses trading due to emergency
Attacker places CLOB orders via validateHandlerOrder (no pause check)
Orders queue at favorable prices during pause
When admin unpauses, orders fill before market adjusts

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-05: Direct swap pricing bounds bypass when afterSwap flag disabled (CP-004)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CP-004 confirmed known pattern. Existing guard exists: afterSwap hook flag must be enabled for bounds enforcement. The pattern is flag-gated enforcement where disabling one flag silently disables a security check set up by another flag. Documented as known issue.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-DP-09: Operator precedence bug in ModuleLiquidity.createPool line 90 (deposit0 | deposit1 == 0)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity 0.8 type system prevents uint256|bool mixing. The expression is parsed as (deposit0 | deposit1) == 0, which is the intended behavior. Compiler enforces type safety.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-01: Settings sync sends raw calldata with initialized=false
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CP-005 confirmed pattern. Hook self-heals by re-fetching from registry when initialized=false. Not a vulnerability - the auto-refetch mechanism makes synced settings ephemeral by design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-03: Disabled pool bypass via cache desync
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By-design cache desync model. Registry NatSpec documents that hook caches must be explicitly synced. Admin config error (not syncing hook) is documented behavior. Tier C impact.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-06: Asymmetric bounds enforcement (pool creation vs swaps)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By design: pool creation checks BOTH tokens' bounds, swaps check per-hook token only. Each hook governs its own token independently. This is the correct architectural model.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-07: Direct swap price distorted by fees (gross vs net input)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Bounds checking uses gross input but AMM uses net input. The margin of error is bounded by the fee percentage. Low impact: cannot exceed fee % distortion, not exploitable for value extraction.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-08: validateHandlerOrder as pricing bounds oracle
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Information leakage is real (binary search to find bounds) but bounds are also visible in events and storage. No economic impact from knowing pricing bounds. Informational at best.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-HR-09: Stale empty pricing bounds in handler validation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By-design cache model. Pricing bounds have no auto-fetch mechanism. Admin must explicitly sync to hook. Documented behavior - not syncing is admin config error.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-DP-01: 100% pool fee on input swaps (asymmetric fee check)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The condition '(inputSwap && >MAX_BPS) || >=MAX_BPS' always catches poolFeeBPS=10000 via the second clause (>=10000). The inputSwap clause is redundant but not exploitable. No asymmetry at the boundary value.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-DP-03: Output swap fee amplification (10000x at hop=9999)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Admin-controlled hop fees. limitAmount check at line 2171 protects users. Amplification is by-design minimum protocol fee enforcement. Compromised fee manager is out of scope (admin-only path).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-DP-05: Hook fee key asymmetry (tokenFor,tokenFor vs tokenFor,tokenFee)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Non-token hook fees are denominated in tokenFor. Store key uses (tokenFor,tokenFor) and correct collection uses same. The asymmetry is an API constraint, not a vulnerability. Hook developers must use tokenFor==tokenFee.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-DP-06: Flags cleared before transfer handler callback
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ENTERED bit prevents reentrancy. Flag clear is necessary for self-delegatecall in executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers. Current handlers don't check SWAP_GUARD_FLAG in callbacks. Latent risk for future handlers only.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R4-DP-07: Division by zero in input swap fee path
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _getPoolFee reverts when poolFeeBPS >= MAX_BPS. Max poolFeeBPS = 9999, max lpFeeBPS = 10000. Max product = 99,990,000 < 100,000,000 (DOUBLE_BPS). Denominator cannot be zero with valid BPS values.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker calls validateHandlerOrder with amountOut=type(uint256).max/2 and amountIn=1, computeRatioX96 overflows returning 0. Since 0 > maxSqrtPriceX96 is always false, the max bound is bypassed. Unlike _validatePricingBounds which checks sqrtPriceX96==0 at line 847, validateHandlerOrder has no such guard.
hypothesis_results.detail: Confirmed. Forge test demonstrates max pricing bound bypass via overflow. Missing sqrtPriceX96==0 check in validateHandlerOrder vs present in _validatePricingBounds.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker calls validateHandlerOrder while tradingIsPaused=true, the function has no pause check. beforeSwap checks via _validateTokenTradingRules at line 117, but validateHandlerOrder skips all trading rules. This means CLOB orders can be placed during trading pauses.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol:117 (only in beforeSwap, NOT in validateHandlerOrder at line 198)
hypothesis_results.detail: Confirmed. Forge test demonstrates trading pause bypass. validateHandlerOrder has no access control and no trading rule enforcement.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a compromised fee manager sets hopFeeBPS=9999, the protocolFeeFromInput formula amplifies shortage by 10000x. User paying 1000 could be charged 10M extra.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:2171 (limitAmount check caps user's maximum payment)
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. limitAmount check protects users. Hop fees are admin-controlled - compromised admin is out of scope per FP pattern #4.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If Solidity parsed deposit0 | deposit1 == 0 as deposit0 | (deposit1 == 0), then deposit0=100 would produce 100 | true = 101 (truthy). But Solidity 0.8 type system prevents uint256 | bool, forcing (deposit0 | deposit1) == 0.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. Solidity 0.8 type system prevents the hypothesized precedence bug. The expression is type-safe.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If setTokenSettings syncs raw calldata with initialized=false, the hook stores initialized=false. On next _getOrFetchTokenSettings, initialized=false triggers re-fetch from registry, getting latest settings. The sync is ephemeral.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. CP-005 confirmed pattern. The auto-refetch mechanism makes synced settings self-healing. Not a vulnerability.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If admin updates registry checkDisabledPools=true without syncing hook, the hook's stale cache (checkDisabledPools=false) skips the pool disabled check. Swaps proceed on disabled pools.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. By-design cache desync. Admin must explicitly sync hook settings. Documented behavior.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a token has beforeSwap enabled but afterSwap disabled, direct swap pricing bounds are never checked. beforeSwap stores amount and returns at line 838-840 without checking. afterSwap is never called.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol: afterSwap hook flag must be enabled for bounds enforcement. CP-004 known pattern.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed as CP-004. Known pattern where flag configuration affects security enforcement. Existing guard (afterSwap flag) prevents exploitation when properly configured.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If pool creation checks both tokens' bounds but swaps check only one, a price could pass swap validation but fail pool creation. This asymmetry could prevent legitimate pool creation.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. Asymmetric enforcement is by design. Each hook governs its own token independently.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If hook charges 10% fee, bounds checking uses gross input but AMM uses net input. Apparent price sqrt(95/100)=0.974 passes max=1.0, but actual economic price sqrt(95/90)=1.027 exceeds max.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol:842 (uses stored gross amount, not net amount)
hypothesis_results.detail: Tested. Fee-sized margin of error confirmed in bounds checking. Impact is low - bounded by fee percentage.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker binary-searches validateHandlerOrder with different amounts, they can reconstruct exact min/max pricing bounds. The function is external view with no access control.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: None - validateHandlerOrder has no access control at AMMStandardHook.sol:207
hypothesis_results.detail: Tested. Information leakage confirmed but impact is informational - bounds visible in events/storage.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If pricing bounds set in registry but not synced to hook, validateHandlerOrder silently skips all price validation (isSet=false). CLOB orders at any price are accepted.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CreatorHookSettingsRegistry cache model (no auto-fetch for pricing bounds)
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. By-design cache model. No auto-fetch for pricing bounds.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a dynamic fee hook returns poolFeeBPS=10000, the check (inputSwap && >MAX_BPS) || >=MAX_BPS always catches 10000 via the second clause. 100% pool fee is blocked for both input and output swaps.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:1717 (>=MAX_BPS second clause always triggers for 10000)
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. No asymmetry at boundary value. The >= clause catches 10000 for both swap types.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If _storeNonTokenHookFees stores fees under hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFor)) but _transferHookFeesByHook withdraws under hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee)), a hook developer calling with tokenFor != tokenFee gets underflow revert. Fees are stranded.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMModule.sol:3016-3018 (store key) vs 3123-3125 (transfer key) - match only when tokenFor==tokenFee
hypothesis_results.detail: Tested. Key asymmetry confirmed. However, non-token hook fees are denominated in tokenFor by design. Correct usage requires tokenFor==tokenFee.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers clears SWAP_GUARD_FLAG at line 3190, the transfer handler callback at line 2251 runs without the flag. A handler checking checkAMMExecutionState(SWAP_GUARD_FLAG) sees false during active swap.
hypothesis_results.detail: Tested. Flag clear confirmed as necessary for self-delegatecall. ENTERED bit still prevents reentrancy. Current handlers don't check SWAP_GUARD_FLAG.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If poolFeeBPS=10000 and lpFeeBPS=10000, denominator becomes 0 causing division by zero. But _getPoolFee reverts when poolFeeBPS>=MAX_BPS, capping it at 9999. Max product = 9999*10000 = 99,990,000 < 100,000,000.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dismissed. _getPoolFee guard prevents poolFeeBPS=10000. Denominator minimum is 10,000 (not zero).

theft_theses.thesis: Exploit validateHandlerOrder overflow to place CLOB orders at infinite prices, bypassing max pricing bounds
theft_theses.victim: Token creators with max-only pricing bounds
theft_theses.asset: Token value through unfavorable CLOB fills

theft_theses.thesis: Place CLOB orders during trading pause via validateHandlerOrder, front-run pause lifting
Bypass direct swap pricing bounds when afterSwap flag disabled
theft_theses.victim: Token creators relying on pricing bounds for direct swaps
theft_theses.asset: Swaps at prices outside intended bounds
